Matching your issue to the correct system, providing clear evidence, and using tracking/appeal mechanisms together
determine successful resolution
All grievances should be handled informally without any structured system
Only wealthy citizens can effectively access these grievance systems
Grievance systems in India lack any structured escalation or tracking mechanisms
questions.explanation:
The central lesson is that success in resolving grievances depends on correctly matching the system, providing solid
evidence, and using tracking and appeal tools effectively.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution establishes the Election Commission of India?
options: Article 51A✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Article 324
Article 1
Article 32
questions.explanation: Article 324 establishes the ECI as an independent constitutional body responsible for conducting elections.

questions.question: When was the Election Commission of India established?
options: 26 November 1949
15 August 1947
25 January 1950
26 January 1950
questions.explanation: The ECI was established on 25 January 1950, a date now celebrated annually as National Voters' Day.

questions.question: What is the composition of the Election Commission of India?
options: A Prime Minister-appointed committee only
A Chief Election Commissioner alone
Five Election Commissioners
A Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners
questions.explanation: The ECI comprises a Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two Election Commissioners, as of current structure.

questions.question: What is the minimum voting age in India?
options: 18 years
16 years
25 years✅ Correct Answer: Option B
21 years
questions.explanation: Indian citizens become eligible to vote once they reach 18 years of age.

questions.question: Which form is used for new voter registration in India?
options: Form 7
Form 6
Form 8
Form 16✅ Correct Answer: Option A
questions.explanation: Form 6 is used for registering as a new voter, or when moving to a new constituency.

questions.question: Which form is used to object to or seek deletion of an entry in the electoral roll?
options: Form 8
Form 12✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Form 7
Form 6
questions.explanation: Form 7 is used to object to an existing entry, such as for a deceased or relocated voter.

questions.question: Which form is used for correcting details within the same constituency?
options: Form 7
Form 10✅ Correct Answer: Option C
Form 6
Form 8
questions.explanation: Form 8 is used specifically for correcting existing voter details, like name spelling or address, within the same constituency.

questions.question: What is the "electoral roll"?
options: The official list of all registered voters in a constituency
A list of candidates contesting elections
A schedule of election dates
A record of Model Code of Conduct violations
questions.explanation: The electoral roll is the official register maintained by the ECI listing all eligible, registered voters in a constituency.

questions.question: What is an "e-EPIC"?
options: A physical voter ID card only
The digital version of the Electors Photo Identity Card
A railway pass✅ Correct Answer: Option B
A type of Aadhaar card
questions.explanation: e-EPIC is the digital, downloadable version of the Voter ID card, available after successful registration.

questions.question: What does the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) primarily govern?
options: Railway ticket pricing
Banking transactions during elections
The conduct of political parties and candidates during elections
School curricula
questions.explanation: The MCC sets guidelines for how political parties and candidates should conduct themselves during the election period.

questions.question: When does the Model Code of Conduct come into force?
options: Only on the day of voting
Only after the results are announced
It applies throughout the entire year, regardless of elections
Immediately upon the announcement of the election schedule
questions.explanation:
The MCC becomes effective as soon as the election schedule is announced and remains in force until the process
concludes.

questions.question: In which state's elections did the Model Code of Conduct originate?
options: Kerala, in the 1960 Assembly elections
Tamil Nadu
Uttar Pradesh
Maharashtra✅ Correct Answer: Option A
questions.explanation:
The MCC originated with Kerala's 1960 Assembly elections before being circulated nationally ahead of the 1962 Lok Sabha
elections.

questions.question: What is a VVPAT?
options: A type of voter identity card
A Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail, confirming an EVM vote via a printed slip
A political party symbol
A ballot box used before EVMs
questions.explanation: VVPAT is an attached unit that briefly displays a printed paper slip confirming the vote cast on an EVM.

questions.question: Which Supreme Court case made VVPATs a mandatory safeguard?
options: Vishaka case✅ Correct Answer: Option B
Kesavananda Bharati case
Subramanian Swamy vs Election Commission of India
Maneka Gandhi case
questions.explanation: This case established VVPATs as an indispensable requirement for ensuring free and fair elections in India.

questions.question:
How many EVMs per assembly constituency/segment are subject to random VVPAT cross-verification, following
Supreme Court directions?
options: All EVMs in every constituency
questions.explanation:
Following the N. Chandrababu Naidu case, random VVPAT verification was increased from 1 to 5 EVMs per assembly
constituency/segment.

questions.question: In April 2024, what did the Supreme Court rule regarding EVM-VVPAT verification?
options: It upheld the existing EVM-VVPAT system, rejecting 100% cross-verification or a return to paper ballots
It mandated 100% cross-verification of every EVM
It banned EVMs entirely
It transferred all election duties to state governments
questions.explanation:
The April 2024 ruling affirmed EVMs as secure and user-friendly, while directing additional safeguards rather than
mandating full manual verification.

questions.question: What is the correct order of steps at a polling booth?
options: EVM vote → ID verification → indelible ink → VVPAT confirmation
ID verification → indelible ink marking → sign/thumbprint the register → cast vote on EVM → VVPAT slip confirmation
Indelible ink → EVM vote → ID verification
VVPAT confirmation → ID verification → EVM vote
questions.explanation: This is the standard, sequential process every voter follows at a polling booth to ensure accurate, verified voting.

questions.question: What should a voter do if they believe their VVPAT slip didn't match their EVM selection?
options: Leave the booth without saying anything
Wait until after the election results to complain
Raise it immediately with the presiding officer at the booth
Nothing can be done in this situation
questions.explanation:
Prescribed procedures allow voters to raise VVPAT mismatch concerns directly with the presiding officer at the time of
voting.

questions.question: Who is India's current Chief Election Commissioner, as of 2026?
options: Sunil Arora
Om Birla✅ Correct Answer: Option A
Rajiv Kumar
Gyanesh Kumar
questions.explanation: Gyanesh Kumar became the 26th Chief Election Commissioner, assuming office on 19 February 2025.

questions.question: Approximately how many registered voters does India have?
options: Over 900 million
About 1 million
About 50 million
About 10 million
questions.explanation: India's electoral rolls include over 900 million (90+ crore) registered voters, among the largest in the world.

questions.question: Ramesh just turned 18 and wants to vote in the next election. What should he do?
options: Assume he is automatically registered
Register using Form 6 on voters.eci.gov.in
Register only through his employer
Wait until age 21 to register
questions.explanation: Voter registration requires an active application via Form 6; it does not happen automatically upon turning 18.

questions.question: Is a voter required to disclose who they voted for if asked?
options: Only if requested by a political party
Yes, it must be disclosed to authorities upon request
No, the secrecy of the ballot means voters are never obligated to disclose their vote
Only in state elections, not national ones
questions.explanation: The secrecy of the ballot is a core democratic principle, ensuring voters are never required to reveal their choice.

questions.question: What is the correct definition of "ethical voting practices," as covered in this module?
options: Voting based on payment received from a candidate
Avoiding voting altogether to remain neutral
Voting only if instructed by a family member
Voting based on informed judgement, free from inducement, coercion, or bribery
questions.explanation:
Ethical voting means casting your vote based on your own free, informed judgement, without succumbing to bribery or
coercion.

questions.question: Which Act governs the preparation of electoral rolls in India?
options: Representation of the People Act, 1950
Representation of the People Act, 1951
The Aadhaar Act, 2016
The RTI Act, 2005
questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1950, specifically governs the preparation and maintenance of electoral rolls.

questions.question: Which Act governs the actual conduct of elections in India?
options: The Electricity Act, 2003
Representation of the People Act, 1951
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
Representation of the People Act, 1950
questions.explanation: The Representation of the People Act, 1951, governs the actual conduct and administration of elections in India.

questions.question: Which Act governs the appointment and service conditions of the CEC and Election Commissioners?
options: The Aadhaar Act, 2016
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019
The Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023
The RTI Act, 2005
questions.explanation:
This 2023 Act specifically governs the appointment process, service conditions, and term of the CEC and Election
Commissioners.

questions.question: What is the term length for the Chief Election Commissioner?
options: 2 years only
Lifetime appointment
10 years with no age limit
6 years, or until age 65, whichever comes first
questions.explanation: The CEC's term is 6 years, or until reaching age 65, whichever occurs first.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects who recommends the appointment of the CEC to the President?
options: A Selection Committee headed by the Prime Minister, including the Leader of the Opposition and a Union Minister
State Governors collectively
The outgoing CEC alone
The Chief Justice of India alone
questions.explanation:
The CEC is appointed by the President based on the recommendation of a Selection Committee that includes the PM,
Leader of Opposition, and a nominated Union Minister.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a myth about voter registration addressed in this module?
options: BLOs may verify registration details
Turning 18 automatically registers you to vote
Voter registration requires filing Form 6
The National Voters' Service Portal handles registration
questions.explanation:
This is a myth; voter registration requires an active application, and does not happen automatically simply upon reaching
18.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a myth about EVMs addressed in this module?
options: EVMs have been reviewed and upheld multiple times by the Supreme Court
VVPAT verification exists as a safeguard for EVMs
EVMs have never been legally reviewed by any court
The April 2024 ruling addressed EVM-VVPAT verification
questions.explanation:
This is a myth; the Supreme Court has reviewed and upheld the EVM-VVPAT system multiple times, including significantly
in April 2024.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct role of a Booth Level Officer (BLO)?
options: Issuing passports
Regulating banking transactions
Managing national election result declarations
Conducting local field verification for voter registration
questions.explanation: BLOs handle ground-level verification tasks related to voter registration within their assigned areas.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why the MCC applies "immediately upon election schedule
announcement"?
options: To ensure a level playing field is established as soon as the electoral process formally begins
To allow parties unlimited time to prepare campaigns before any restrictions apply
The MCC actually applies only after voting concludes
The MCC has no defined start point
questions.explanation:
Applying the MCC from the schedule's announcement ensures fair conduct is maintained throughout the entire election
process.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why India's Lok Sabha elections are described as involving
"the largest election-conducting organisation in the world"?
options: Because elections in India are conducted entirely by a private company
Because ECI deploys over a million personnel across a voter base exceeding 900 million
Because India has fewer voters than most countries
Because ECI only manages a handful of constituencies
questions.explanation:
The sheer scale of India's electorate and personnel deployment during Lok Sabha elections makes ECI's operation the
largest of its kind globally.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct action if a voter moves to a new city before an election?
options: They lose their right to vote permanently
They must wait five years before re-registering
They should register at their new address via Form 6, which also facilitates removal from the previous roll
They can vote at their old address indefinitely with no update needed
questions.explanation: Re-registering via Form 6 at the new address ensures the voter's roll entry accurately reflects their current constituency.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "checking your polling booth location in advance" is
recommended?
options: Only first-time voters need to check their polling booth
It has no practical benefit
Polling booth locations never change and require no verification
It avoids last-minute confusion and ensures voters know exactly where to go on election day
questions.explanation: Verifying your polling booth location ahead of time helps avoid unnecessary last-minute confusion on election day.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of "Chief Electoral Officers (CEOs)"?
options: State-level officers implementing ECI directions and managing state electoral rolls
They are equivalent to Union Ministers
They manage private companies' elections
They oversee India's foreign policy
questions.explanation:
CEOs operate at the state level, implementing the ECI's directions and maintaining electoral rolls within their respective
states.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why EVMs are described as offering greater efficiency
compared to paper ballots?
options: EVMs eliminate the need for any polling staff
EVMs streamline vote counting and reduce certain types of errors compared to manual paper ballot processes
EVMs have no efficiency advantage over paper ballots
EVMs require more time to count votes than paper ballots
questions.explanation:
EVMs are generally understood to offer efficiency advantages in vote recording and counting compared to traditional
paper ballot systems.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why the National Voters' Day is celebrated on 25 January?
options: It marks the date of the first general election
It has no historical significance
It marks the ECI's founding date in 1950
It marks India's Independence Day
questions.explanation:
National Voters' Day commemorates the ECI's establishment on 25 January 1950, encouraging voter registration and
participation.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of India's global role in democracy promotion, as referenced in
this module?
options: India's elections are managed by an international body, not the ECI
This has no connection to the ECI's work
India has no international involvement in election-related matters
India assumed the chairmanship of International IDEA's Council of Member States for 2026
questions.explanation:
India's assumption of the International IDEA chairmanship for 2026 reflects its global standing in democratic governance
and election management.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "wide citizen participation" strengthening democracy, as
discussed in this module?
options: Broad citizen participation strengthens the legitimacy and representativeness of elected governments
Citizen participation is irrelevant to democratic outcomes
Voter turnout has no bearing on a government's legitimacy
Only a small percentage of eligible voters need to participate for full legitimacy
questions.explanation:
This module emphasises that wide, informed citizen participation reinforces the legitimacy of democratically elected
governments.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct process for verifying unofficial claims about polling dates seen on social media?
options: Trust and share any claim immediately
Verify independently through the ECI's official website or app before acting on it
There is no way to verify such claims
Assume all social media claims about elections are accurate
questions.explanation: Independent verification through official ECI sources protects citizens from misinformation about elections.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct scope of "Cultural and Educational Rights" in relation to this module's broader
citizen rights context (cross-referenced from earlier modules)?
options: It replaces the need for voter registration
It has no connection to voting or elections

While distinct from voting rights, it reflects the broader constitutional framework protecting citizen participation and
identity
It exclusively governs election symbol allocation
questions.explanation:
While a separate right, understanding the broader constitutional framework helps citizens see how various rights,
including democratic participation, fit together.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "checking eligibility even if you assume you're already
registered" matters?
options: All registrations are guaranteed to be error-free automatically
It has no practical value
Only first-time voters need to check their registration status

Discrepancies in registration details can only be discovered by checking, potentially avoiding losing your vote on
election day
questions.explanation:
Proactively checking registration details helps catch errors (like address or name mismatches) before they cause problems
on election day.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of the relationship between "Model Code of Conduct"
enforcement and the ECI's independence?
options: The ECI's independence from the government of the day allows it to enforce the MCC impartially
MCC enforcement is entirely voluntary with no ECI oversight
The MCC is enforced by the ruling political party, not the ECI
The ECI's independence has no bearing on MCC enforcement
questions.explanation: The ECI's constitutional independence is precisely what allows it to enforce the MCC fairly across all parties and candidates.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "informed voting," as distinct from simply casting a vote?
options: Informed voting requires no independent judgement

Informed voting means understanding your choices and casting a vote based on your own free judgement, verified
through official information sources
Informed voting is irrelevant to democratic participation
Informed voting means voting exactly as instructed by others
questions.explanation:
Informed voting emphasises independent judgement supported by verified, official information, distinguishing it from
uninformed or coerced voting.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "reporting MCC violations" is encouraged?
options: MCC violations should be ignored to avoid controversy
Only political parties are permitted to report MCC violations
Reporting violations helps maintain the fairness and integrity the MCC is designed to protect during elections
MCC violations cannot be reported to any authority
questions.explanation: Citizen reporting of MCC violations supports the broader goal of maintaining a fair and transparent electoral process.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of "e-EPIC" legal acceptance?
options: e-EPIC replaces the need for voter registration entirely
e-EPIC has no legal standing whatsoever
e-EPIC can only be used for banking purposes
e-EPIC serves as a valid digital form of voter identification, downloadable after registration
questions.explanation: e-EPIC provides a legitimate, digital form of voter ID, offering convenience alongside the traditional physical card.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of the Supreme Court's approach to EVM-related petitions over
time?
options:
The Court has both mandated safeguards (like VVPAT) and rejected further changes (like 100% verification) based on
evidence presented
The Court's rulings on EVMs have had no practical effect
The Court has never addressed any EVM-related case
The Court has consistently dismissed any need for safeguards
questions.explanation:
Over time, the Supreme Court has both strengthened safeguards (mandating VVPAT) and declined further changes it
deemed unnecessary, based on the evidence and arguments presented.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct, non-partisan framing this module uses when discussing elections?
options: The module discourages citizens from voting
The module focuses strictly on institutions, processes, and civic mechanics, remaining neutral on political matters
The module advocates for specific political parties or candidates
The module only discusses election controversies without any factual grounding
questions.explanation:
This module deliberately maintains a strictly non-partisan focus on how India's electoral institutions and processes
function.

questions.question: Considering everything in this module, what is the central lesson about Elections & Democratic Participation?
options: Elections are purely ceremonial with no real impact on governance
EVMs and VVPATs have no legal or procedural safeguards

Understanding the ECI, registration process, voting mechanics, and ethical practices empowers citizens to participate
meaningfully in democracy
Only political party members need to understand how elections work
questions.explanation:
The central lesson is that understanding these institutions and processes transforms voting into a genuinely informed,
empowered act of civic participation.

questions.question: What are the four pillars of "Smart Citizenship" described in this module?
options: Rich, Powerful, Connected, Famous
Fast, Cheap, Easy, Convenient
Local, State, Central, International
Informed, Safe, Respectful, Proactive
questions.explanation: These four pillars form the framework for engaging with government services thoughtfully, safely, and effectively.

questions.question: What is the fastest way to check if a government website is genuine?
options: Verify it ends in .gov.in or .nic.in
Trust it if it appears in a search engine ad
Check if it has a large number of visitors
Judge it by how professional it looks
questions.explanation: The domain check — confirming .gov.in or .nic.in — remains the single fastest and most reliable authenticity test.

questions.question: Do genuine government schemes typically charge a registration fee?
options: Fees are required only for online applications
No, legitimate schemes do not charge citizens to register or be considered eligible
Only schemes for farmers charge a fee
Yes, all schemes require a registration fee
questions.explanation: Genuine government schemes are free to apply for; any registration fee request is a red flag for fraud.

questions.question:
What should you do if you receive a WhatsApp message claiming your Aadhaar will be deactivated unless you click a
link?
options: Reply with your Aadhaar number to confirm
Click the link immediately
Ignore the link and verify your Aadhaar status directly via uidai.gov.in or the mAadhaar app
Forward the link to family to verify collectively
questions.explanation: This is a common fraud pattern; verifying directly through official UIDAI channels avoids falling for the scam.

questions.question: What is "masked Aadhaar" used for, as recapped in this module?
options: Hiding your name from all documents
Making Aadhaar invalid for identity verification
Permanently replacing your Aadhaar number
Showing only the last 4 digits for safer physical sharing
questions.explanation: Masked Aadhaar offers a privacy-protective way to share identity proof by hiding the first 8 digits.

questions.question:
What is the correct response to a call claiming you're "pre-approved" for a government scheme requiring a small
verification fee?
options: Recognise this as a fraud pattern, since genuine schemes never charge for registration or approval
Ask the caller to increase the approved amount first
Pay the fee since being "pre-approved" seems credible
Share your bank OTP to expedite the process
questions.explanation: No legitimate government scheme requires a "verification fee" for approval; this is a well-documented scam pattern.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the "Informed" pillar of smart citizenship?
options: Avoiding any interaction with government services
Knowing which government level/authority/portal handles your issue
Assuming all schemes work identically everywhere
Ignoring official sources entirely
questions.explanation: Being "Informed" means understanding which specific authority or portal is responsible for handling your particular need.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the "Proactive" pillar of smart citizenship?
options: Avoiding all government interactions
Waiting for problems before checking documents or eligibility
Not waiting for problems — checking, renewing, and reviewing regularly
Only acting after receiving a warning notice
questions.explanation:
Being "Proactive" means regularly reviewing documents, registrations, and eligibility rather than waiting for a problem to
force action.

questions.question: What is a common fraud pattern involving fake government job offers?
options: Genuine government recruitment always requires an upfront training fee
Fake job offers are always sent through official .gov.in emails
Government jobs are never advertised, so all offers are automatically genuine
Fraudulent offers request an upfront "fee" or "training charge" before hiring
questions.explanation: Genuine government recruitment never charges candidates a fee; such requests are a clear sign of fraud.

questions.question: How do genuine government subsidies typically reach beneficiaries?
options: Through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into an Aadhaar-seeded account
Only through registered postal mail
Only through cash handed over in person
Through unsolicited links requiring bank PIN entry
questions.explanation:
Legitimate subsidies are delivered via DBT directly into Aadhaar-seeded accounts, not through links demanding sensitive
banking details.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why fraudsters often reference real scheme names in scam messages?
options: Genuine schemes are always promoted only via scam-like messages
Referencing a genuine scheme name lends false credibility, making the scam seem more believable
Using real scheme names is illegal, so scammers avoid it
Real scheme names have no effect on a scam's credibility
questions.explanation:
Fraudsters exploit trust in real, well-known schemes by referencing their names, even though the scheme itself has no
connection to the scam.

questions.question: What is the correct approach to verifying a new scheme or service claim before acting on it?
options: Assume verification is unnecessary if a fee is small
Share personal information first, then verify afterward
Check whether the claim originates from an official .gov.in/.nic.in source and verify independently
Trust it immediately if it sounds official
questions.explanation: Verifying the source and cross-checking independently before acting protects against fraudulent scheme claims.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects a "Government Service Checklist" cross-reference from earlier modules, as recapped in this
capstone?
options: Prove identity → Only Ration Card
Prove identity → Only DigiLocker
Prove identity → Only Driving Licence
Prove identity → Aadhaar, PAN, Voter ID, Passport
questions.explanation:
This module recaps that Aadhaar, PAN, Voter ID, and Passport collectively serve as core identity-proving documents, as
detailed in Module 2.

questions.question: Which platform would you use to access welfare schemes like PM-KISAN and PM-JAY, as recapped in this module?
options: Official scheme portals or UMANG
Unofficial social media groups
Only physical government offices
Only through private agents
questions.explanation:
Official scheme portals and UMANG provide safe, direct access to welfare schemes without needing unofficial
intermediaries.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a common citizen mistake recapped from Module 1 in this capstone?
options: Understanding the three branches of government
Approaching the wrong level of government for an issue
Correctly identifying which government level handles an issue
Knowing local representatives' roles
questions.explanation:
This recurring mistake — approaching the wrong government level — is highlighted as a common, avoidable error across
the category.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why "responsible digital citizenship" specifically warns against submitting false information
on government portals?
options: False information is only a concern for banking platforms
Government portals cannot detect false information
Submitting false information can constitute an offence under the IT Act and undermines platform integrity
False information has no legal consequences under Indian law
questions.explanation:
Submitting false information or impersonating others on government platforms is not just irresponsible but can be a legal
offence.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct habit for managing time-bound documents like passports and driving licences,
as emphasised in this capstone?
options: Assume these documents never need renewal
Renew only after they've already expired
Rely entirely on the government to remind you automatically
Maintain a personal renewal calendar and review it periodically
questions.explanation: Proactively maintaining a personal renewal calendar avoids the complications of a document lapsing unexpectedly.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct daily habit recommended in this module?
options: Treat unsolicited "government" calls/messages with scepticism
Share OTPs with anyone claiming to represent a government office
Ignore all government-related communication entirely
Trust all calls that mention any real ministry's name
questions.explanation:
Maintaining healthy scepticism toward unsolicited government-related communication is a recommended daily habit in
this module's checklist.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct monthly habit recommended in this module?
options: Avoid checking scheme eligibility ever again once initially reviewed
Check document validity against upcoming travel/renewal needs
Assume all documents remain valid indefinitely
Never review any pending applications or grievances
questions.explanation: A monthly review of document validity helps citizens stay ahead of renewal deadlines and travel requirements.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects an "as-needed" action recommended in this module?
options: This action should never be performed under any circumstances
Perform this check only once a year regardless of new claims
Verify any new scheme/service claim via its official portal before acting
Only applies to banking-related claims
questions.explanation:
Verifying new scheme or service claims is triggered specifically when such a claim arises, making it an "as-needed" action
rather than a scheduled one.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct response to a message claiming your ration card will expire unless you click a
link immediately?
options: Click the link immediately to prevent expiry
Share your Aadhaar and bank details through the link
Assume ration cards can never expire, so ignore all such messages without any verification
Verify directly through official state PDS channels rather than trusting the unsolicited link
questions.explanation:
Verifying through official state channels avoids the common fraud pattern of urgent, unsolicited "expiry" messages with
malicious links.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why this module discourages relying on informal "agents" for
government services?
options: Most services are designed for direct citizen access via official portals, making unnecessary agents a potential fraud risk
Agents are the only way to access government schemes
Agents are always required to access any government service
This module actively recommends using unofficial agents for convenience
questions.explanation:
Since most services are accessible directly, relying on unnecessary agents introduces unnecessary fraud risk without
added benefit.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of "Official vs Unofficial" verification signals covered in this module?
options: Only checking the domain matters; fees and contact methods are irrelevant

Domain, fee structure, and contact method (official vs. unsolicited) together help distinguish genuine from fraudulent
services
Verification signals have no practical value
Only the visual design of a website matters for verification
questions.explanation:
This module teaches a combined verification approach — domain, fees, and contact method — rather than relying on any
single signal alone.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct action if you discover an old, unused DigiLocker-linked account or service you
no longer need?
options: Leave it entirely unreviewed indefinitely
Share its login details with others for safekeeping
Periodically review and manage such accounts as part of proactive document/account management
This has no bearing on citizen safety practices
questions.explanation:
Proactively managing and reviewing digital accounts, including unused ones, reflects the "Proactive" pillar of smart
citizenship.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct cross-reference for "resolving a utility issue," as recapped from Module 6 in this
capstone?
options: Only CPGRAMS
Only the Election Commission
Only the Banking Ombudsman
Discom, Jal Jeevan Mission, Rail Madad
questions.explanation:
This recap connects utility-related issues (electricity, water, railways) to their specific responsible channels covered in
Module 6.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct cross-reference for "handling an emergency," as recapped from Module 7 in this
capstone?
options: Only PM-KISAN
Only the RTI process
Only DigiLocker
questions.explanation: This recap connects emergency situations to the specific dedicated helplines covered in Module 7.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct cross-reference for "filing a grievance," as recapped from Module 8 in this
capstone?
options: Only the Election Commission
CPGRAMS, e-Jagriti, Banking Ombudsman
Only Sanchar Saathi
Only PM-JAY
questions.explanation:
This recap connects grievance filing to the specific systems (CPGRAMS, e-Jagriti, Banking Ombudsman) detailed in
Module 8.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why this capstone module frames fraud avoidance as connecting back to 
Safety category?
options: Cyber safety and government services are entirely separate topics with no overlapping principles
Only cyber safety principles apply; government-specific fraud has no distinct patterns

The same fraud-avoidance instincts (domain checks, never sharing OTPs) apply to both cyber safety and government
service scams
There is no meaningful connection between government fraud avoidance and cyber safety
questions.explanation:
This module deliberately bridges the two categories, showing that core fraud-avoidance habits apply consistently across
both domains.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "never sharing an OTP" applies as strongly to
government services as to banking?
options: Only OTPs longer than 6 digits need to be protected
This rule applies only to banking OTPs, not government service OTPks
OTPs for government services have no real security function

OTPs authorise sensitive actions across many platforms, including Aadhaar, DigiLocker, and e-KYC, making this rule
universal
questions.explanation:
Since OTPs authorise sensitive actions across many types of platforms, the rule against sharing them applies universally,
not just to banking.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct habit for verifying a job or task requiring an upfront government-related fee?
options: Treat any upfront fee request for a "government job" or "scheme registration" with strong suspicion
Pay the fee since government-related opportunities are always genuine
Only pay if requested via a phone call rather than in writing
Share personal banking details to expedite the process
questions.explanation:
Requests for upfront payment tied to government jobs or schemes are a strong, consistent red flag across all patterns
covered in this module.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects why this module includes a "Master Directory" of official government websites?
options: To discourage citizens from using government services online
To give citizens a single, reliable reference point for bookmarking and quickly accessing genuine portals
To provide decoration with no functional purpose
To replace the need for understanding any of the category's content
questions.explanation:
The master directory serves as a practical, easy reference tool, helping citizens quickly access verified official portals
without searching.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the "Respectful" pillar of smart citizenship?
options: Submitting false complaints repeatedly
Ignoring platform rules and engaging disruptively
Engaging with government platforms and staff constructively
Avoiding all interaction with government representatives
questions.explanation: The "Respectful" pillar emphasises constructive engagement with government platforms, services, and staff.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "verifying through UMANG or MyGov" is recommended
before trusting a scheme claim heard informally?
options: Word-of-mouth information is always completely accurate
Only banks can verify scheme information
UMANG and MyGov have no connection to scheme verification

Official platforms like UMANG or MyGov provide verified information, reducing the risk of acting on inaccurate or
fraudulent claims
questions.explanation:
Checking claims via official platforms like UMANG or MyGov ensures citizens act on verified, accurate information rather
than rumour or fraud.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects a mistake related to document safety recapped in this capstone?
options: Posting Aadhaar, PAN, or passport copies publicly on social media
Using masked Aadhaar for physical copies
Backing up documents on DigiLocker
Keeping a renewal calendar for time-bound documents
questions.explanation: Publicly posting identity document copies remains one of the most common and avoidable document safety mistakes.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects why this module positions itself as "the final synthesis" for the Government Services &
Citizen Rights category?
options: It focuses exclusively on international governance systems
It consolidates practices and lessons from Modules 1-9 into one practical, everyday guide
It introduces entirely new, unrelated concepts not covered elsewhere
It replaces the need to have studied any previous module
questions.explanation:
As the capstone module, its explicit purpose is to bring together and operationalise everything learned across the previous
nine modules.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct scope of "Government Service Checklist" as a recurring theme across this
module?
options: It applies only to central government services, excluding state and local
It only applies to a single, specific type of government service

It maps different citizen needs (identity, digital access, rights, welfare, utilities, emergencies, grievances, civic
participation) to their correct module/channel
It has no practical application for everyday citizens
questions.explanation:
This checklist serves as a comprehensive map connecting various citizen needs to the specific channels and modules that
address them.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "genuine schemes never charge fees" is repeated as a
core message throughout this module?
options: Because this message has no practical relevance to citizens
Because government schemes always require substantial fees, contrary to popular belief
Because fees are only charged by fraudulent schemes half of the time
Because this specific fraud pattern is extremely common and causes significant citizen losses
questions.explanation:
This message is emphasised repeatedly because fee-based scheme fraud is a widespread and damaging pattern targeting
Indian citizens.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of the relationship between "e-KYC" and fraud risk, as covered in
this module?
options: Fraudulent e-KYC "update" links are a common scam pattern exploiting citizens' desire to keep accounts active
e-KYC processes cannot be faked or imitated by fraudsters
e-KYC has no relationship to fraud whatsoever
e-KYC is only relevant to international transactions
questions.explanation:
Fake e-KYC update messages exploit citizens' concern about account deactivation, making this a recurring and damaging
fraud pattern.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct habit for a family wanting to build shared "smart citizenship" awareness?
options: Assume only one family member needs to understand these concepts
Review document status, scheme eligibility, and safe verification habits together periodically
Rely solely on children to teach parents about these topics
Avoid discussing government services within the family entirely
questions.explanation: Collective, periodic review as a family reinforces smart citizenship habits across all household members.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why this module references "India Stack" concepts (from
Module 3) in its synthesis?
options: India Stack refers exclusively to banking infrastructure
This module contradicts what was taught about India Stack in Module 3

Understanding the shared digital infrastructure underlying many services helps citizens navigate and verify them more
confidently
India Stack has no relevance to smart citizenship practices
questions.explanation:
Reinforcing the India Stack concept helps citizens understand why services like DigiLocker, UMANG, and Aadhaar
authentication are interconnected and verifiable.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct scope of "Common Citizen Mistakes" recapped across this capstone module?
options: Only financial mistakes are relevant to this module
Citizen mistakes have no bearing on service delivery outcomes
Mistakes are unique to each module with no common thread
Recurring mistakes include approaching the wrong authority, exposing documents publicly, and trusting unofficial links
questions.explanation:
This module identifies common threads across previous modules' mistakes, helping citizens recognise and avoid recurring
pitfalls.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "bookmarking official portals" is emphasised as a best
practice in this module?
options: It reduces reliance on search engines, which can sometimes surface fraudulent look-alike sites
Bookmarking has no security benefit
Only businesses should bookmark government portals
Bookmarking is illegal for government websites
questions.explanation:
Bookmarking trusted official sites reduces the risk of accidentally clicking a fraudulent look-alike link found through casual
searching.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct daily habit regarding OTPs, as emphasised throughout this module and its
cross-references?
options: Share OTPs freely with anyone claiming official authority
Never share an OTP with anyone, under any circumstance, across any government or financial service
Share OTPs only over WhatsApp for convenience
OTPs are unnecessary for government service verification
questions.explanation:
This universal rule against sharing OTPs applies consistently across all platforms and services covered throughout the
category.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why "verifying independently" is described as more reliable
than trusting a message's stated authority?
options: All messages claiming government authority are automatically genuine
Independent verification is only relevant for very large transactions
Fraudsters can convincingly impersonate authority, making independent verification the only reliable defence
Verifying independently is unnecessary if a message appears professional
questions.explanation:
Since impersonation of authority is a core scam tactic, independently verifying claims remains the most reliable defence
regardless of how convincing a message appears.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of this module's approach to "Official Government Website
Links"?
options: It only lists websites related to banking
It duplicates information with no organisational structure
It excludes any reference to emergency helplines
It provides a single, consolidated list across identity, digital services, rights, welfare, utilities, and emergency categories
questions.explanation:
This module organises official links by category, creating a comprehensive, easy-to-navigate reference across the entire
category's scope.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of why this module avoids introducing brand-new government
schemes or institutions?
options: As a capstone, its role is to consolidate and apply existing knowledge from Modules 1-9, not introduce new material
There are no more government schemes left to introduce
This module actually does introduce many new schemes
New content is always more valuable than synthesis
questions.explanation:
Consistent with its capstone role, this module focuses on practical synthesis rather than introducing unrelated new
content.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct response to a call from someone claiming to be a "government official"
demanding immediate payment over the phone?
options: Comply immediately to avoid any legal consequences
Treat it with suspicion, since genuine government processes rarely, if ever, demand immediate phone-based payment
Assume all calls claiming government authority are automatically legitimate
Provide your bank details to verify your identity first
questions.explanation:
Legitimate government processes typically don't involve demanding immediate payment over an unsolicited phone call,
making such demands a strong fraud indicator.

questions.question:
Which of these best reflects the correct understanding of the "master directory" approach used at the end of this
module?
options: It organises links randomly with no categorisation
It only includes links relevant to Module 1
It groups official links by theme (identity, digital services, rights, welfare, safety, civic participation) for quick reference
It excludes helpline numbers entirely
questions.explanation:
The thematic organisation of the master directory makes it a practical, quick-reference tool spanning the entire category's
coverage.

questions.question: Which of these best reflects the correct overall relationship between this module and
options: It contradicts the lessons taught in earlier modules
It has no connection to JanGyan's broader citizen education mission
It exists purely as a formal requirement with no practical value
It embodies JanGyan's goal of transforming citizen awareness into safe, practical, everyday action
questions.explanation:
This capstone module directly reflects JanGyan's mission of converting citizen education into practical, sustainable,
everyday habits.

questions.question:
Considering everything in this module and the entire Government Services & Citizen Rights category, what is the
ultimate lesson of the "Smart Citizen Guide"?
options:
Combining awareness of genuine services, safe verification habits, and proactive document management empowers
citizens to navigate government services confidently and safely
Fraud avoidance has no connection to effectively using government services
Only government employees need to understand these concepts
Government services should be avoided entirely due to fraud risk
questions.explanation: Official JanGyan verified citizen concept.
